messages:
sara: FYI we're kicking off the v2 batching rollout today 03:30 UTC. Quiet window 2h. Canary: global 2% -> 10% -> 100%. Heads-up: default `batch_size` bumped 4->8 to improve tokens/sec. Watch RPS-based limits and CDN rate-limiters. Call hold if we see 429s or quota trips. :loud_sound:

deploybot: Scheduled rollout: 
- service: request-proxy
- image: ghcr.redwood/proxy:release-v2.3-batching
- rollout-id: rb-6215001234
- step1 pct=2 at 03:35 UTC
- preflight: smoke + e2e passed 2026-03-21T00:45Z

riley: Quick Q  what's our headroom for RPS on the CDN layer? Some tenants are close.

jamie: CDN quota per-tenant is 1200 req/min currently. That's per-req (not token). If batch_size doubles, RPS might double for same token volume. We had telemetry showing enterprise tenants at ~50% headroom at peak.

kevin: Ops-runbook thresholds: 429 > 0.5% sustained 5m -> pause; 5xx >1% -> abort. Also check 4xx client errors.

--- (canary window) ---

deploybot: Canary step1 started (global 2%): rb-6215001234-step1

ops-runner: Seeing a surge in 429s for tenant "alpha-corp" 03:38 UTC — jumping to 3.2% (baseline 0.1%). Looks like CDN rejecting requests.

engtools-bot: Quick metrics dump: 
- alpha-corp reqs/min pre-change: ~900
- post-change: ~1700
- 429s coming from cdn-edge-us-east
- p50 latency unchanged, token throughput up ~1.9x

kevin: Confirming suspicion: batching increased requests/sec for customers that fan out many small requests. CDN enforces req/min, not tokens. Options: A) roll back image B) throttle at proxy (lower batch_size) C) request quota bump from CDN.

riley: CDN quota bump will take hours and needs approvals. Prefer B if it's quick.

jamie: We have a runtime config flag `batching.max_size` that can be adjusted without image rollback. We can set per-tenant override for alpha-corp or globally for canary.

ops-runner: Ops can flip runtime config now. Proposal: set `batching.max_size=4` for canary group and alpha-corp override to 2 until we validate. Then monitor 10m.

sara: Sounds reasonable. Avoid a full rollback if mitigation is quick. Proceed with per-canary override first, alpha override if needed.

deploybot: Applying runtime override: `batching.max_size=4` for rollout rb-6215001234-step1 at 03:41 UTC. Applying per-tenant override alpha-corp -> 2 at 03:42 UTC.

ops-runner: After change, alpha-corp 429s dropped to 0.15% within 60s. Global canary 429s back to baseline.

kevin: Great. Recommendation: pause progression for one canary window (10m) to validate across other multi-fanout tenants. Also open infra ticket to change CDN quota model (tokens-aware) or add tenant-classes to increase RPS for heavy-token customers.

jamie: Filed infra ticket: https://infra.internal/ticket/9872 "CDN quota: make quota token-aware or add high-RPS class". Also added an item to release notes about batching implications.

support-bot: Support notified: "v2 batching rollout paused at step1 due to CDN 429s for some enterprise tenants; temporary per-tenant and canary batching caps applied. Monitoring ongoing."

sara: Thanks. Ops, please keep an eye for any additional tenants with fanout patterns. If we see any new tenant 429 >0.5% for 5m, execute rollback plan: pin header -> rollback image -> notify customers.

ops-runner: Will monitor. Resume schedule: if stable at 03:52 UTC we'll move to 10% at 04:00 UTC. Otherwise escalate.

riley: For postmortem note: consider adding a test that simulates token-preserving but RPS-increasing workload so we catch this in staging.

kevin: Added test task to QA board: "simulate high-fanout clients for batching".

sara: Postmortem + follow-ups scheduled 09:30 UTC tomorrow. For now: rollout paused (safe mode) with batching caps applied. rb-6215001234 paused at step1 by ops-runner. :white_check_mark:
